To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the community health extension worker‐led HIV testing and linkage programme in Uganda increased the number of people tested for HIV, and increased the proportion of HIV‐positive people accessing HIV treatment.

the CHW‐based HIV testing and linkage programme was effective in increasing HIV testing and linkage rates in southwestern Uganda, but the scale‐up of the CHW‐programme was associated with lower linkage rates.

(1) community‐based HIV testing and linkage programs in Uganda can be scaled up to reach a substantial proportion of the population and (2) community‐based testing and linkage programs can be scaled up with minimal loss in the quality of the services provided.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel, highly efficient, and cost‐effective method of HIV testing and linkage‐to‐care in rural Uganda, using community‐health‐extension‐worker‐led home‐based testing and linkage‐in‐care (HIV‐HOTLINC) services.
the following question: how can we improve the quality and efficiency of HIV care in Uganda?
the role of community health extension workers in expanding HIV testing and linkage of newly diagnosed individuals to HIV care in southwestern Uganda.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of community‐based health extension workers is an effective and sustainable strategy for expanding HIV testing and linkage into care in rural southwestern Uganda.
community‐based HIV‐testing‐and‐treatment programmes can expand HIV‐testing‐coverage, increase linkage to HIV‐care, and reduce mortality in resource‐limited settings.

the community‐based HIV testing strategy is an effective and efficient strategy to reach and diagnose the large number of people living with HIV who are unaware of their status, and that the community health extension worker is an effective and sustainable cadre of community‐based health care workers for this purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the CHWs were able to identify HIV positive people, link them to care, and that the CHWs could be effective in a large-scale program.
we have shown that community‐based HIV care is feasible, effective, and scalable in Uganda.
we have shown that CHWs can effectively identify HIV‐positive individuals in the community and link them into care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
community‐based HIV testing and linkage‐to‐care programmes can be successfully scaled up to reach large numbers of people in rural Uganda.
community health extension workers can play an effective role in expanding HIV testing, linkage to care, and retention.
community‐based programmes can be scaled‐up in rural settings with a relatively low cost per person tested and linkage to care.
